concepts.def: Scrambling data so only key holders can read it.
Restricting users to only the data they need.
Hired hackers test a system's defences.
Flooding a server so real users cannot connect.
Sneaking SQL into a form to attack a database.

walkthroughs.body_html: Something you know (password) + something you have (phone code) + something you are (fingerprint). Even if a password leaks, the attacker still can't log in.
HTTPS encrypts the data between your browser and the server. Anyone snooping sees gibberish without the key. WhatsApp uses end-to-end encryption so even the server can't read messages.
A student can read their grades but not edit them. A teacher can edit grades for their class only. An admin can manage all users. This is the principle of least privilege.
